learning_outcomes.text: Ability to apply knowledge in practice
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations
Ability to analyze and evaluate the social and environmental impact of technical solutions
Ability to consider environmental factors in decision-making
SOS2 - Competence in the sustainable use of resources and in the prevention of negative impacts on the natural and social environment.
SOS4 - Competence in the application of ethical principles related to sustainability values in personal and professional behavior.
Understand the context and classification of the main thermal equipment and machines
Understand mass and energy balances in thermal equipment
Understand the calculation and analysis of simple combustion processes
Understand the energy calculation of power generation and refrigeration cycles
Understand the operation of endothermic and exothermic engines
Know how to express and calculate energy balances and efficiencies of endothermic and exothermic engines
Understand the applications in electricity generation and cogeneration of endothermic and exothermic engines

syllabus_topics: 2 Thermal Equipment. Heat exchangers: definitions, classification, uses and operational aspects. Logarithmic mean temperature difference calculation method. Thermal effectiveness and NTU value calculation method. Boilers: definitions, classification, uses and operational aspects.

3 Cold production with a mechanical compression cycle. Fundamental parts and general description. Energy balances in the plant. Refrigerants. Properties and uses. Historical development. Calculation of a simple cycle. Sankey diagram. Efficiencies. Specific consumptions.

4 Work production with a Rankine cycle. Fundamental parts and general description of a power plant with a Rankine cycle. Energy balances in the plant. Simple Rankine cycle, Rankine cycle with superheating, Rankine cycle with reheating, Regenerative Rankine cycle. Combinations of the above. Sankey diagram. Efficiencies. Specific consumptions.

5 Work production with a Brayton cycle. Fundamental parts and general description of a power plant with a Brayton cycle. Energy balances in the plant. Simple Brayton cycle, Brayton cycle with reheating, Brayton cycle with intercooling. Regenerative Brayton cycle. Combinations of the above. Sankey diagram. Efficiencies. Specific consumptions.
6 Combined cycle. Fundamental parts and general description of a power plant with a combined cycle. Energy balances in the plant. Sankey diagram. Efficiencies. Specific consumptions.
7 Combustion. Fuels. Conventional sources of thermal energy. Properties and characteristics of fuels. Oxidizers. Mass and energy balance of a combustion process. Efficiency of a combustion process.

8 Reciprocating internal combustion engines. Definition, historical background, main elements (ICICE), fixed parts, moving parts, fundamental definitions, classification criteria. Work cycle phases, 2 and 4 strokes, main differences between spark-ignition and diesel engines.

1.9 Thermodynamic (theoretical) cycles of reciprocating internal combustion engines. Review of thermodynamics, types of cycles, theoretical Otto cycle, theoretical Diesel cycle, Atkinson cycle. Calculation of values for each point of the cycle and its thermal efficiency, comparison of the three cycles. Basic concepts: Indicated and effective power. Efficiencies. Differences between real and theoretical cycles, 4t and 2t, Pumping power. Losses. Intake and exhaust. Volumetric efficiency, valves, distribution systems, supercharging, scavenging, exhaust gas recirculation.
